title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Rule on the Full-Time Hours Threshold for Weekly Payments on New Claims
content:
**(1)** For a weekly payment on Unemployment Benefit Claims, the full-time hours threshold governing the week — both the hours at or above which the week pays nothing and the hours against which the low, mid and part-week fractions of the week's hours are measured — is 36 hours (the new federal threshold) when the separation recorded on the claim is a federal separation and the claim is fewer than 182 days old.

**(2)** It is 34 hours (the new-claim threshold) when the separation is of any other kind and the claim is fewer than 182 days old.

**(3)** Any other weekly payment uses the program's full-time hours threshold.

**(4)** The age of the claim is the number of calendar days from the claim effective date to the handling date.

## Conditions in combination

| Separation recorded on the claim | Age of the claim | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| Federal separation | Fewer than 182 days | 36 hours |
| Any other separation | Fewer than 182 days | 34 hours |
| Any | 182 days or more | The program's full-time hours threshold |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

| Separation | Age of the claim | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| Federal separation | 181 days | 36 hours |
| Federal separation | 182 days | The program's threshold |
| Lack of work | 60 days | 34 hours |
